title: Tech Note: 4D V6 Cross Platform Strategies
author: David Hartje

historical_commentary.text: The extracted text for this asset did not contain the actual Tech Note content — it resolved instead to Tech Note 96-50, 'Installing and Configuring Mac and PC Remote Access to a Windows NT-based 4D Server,' an unrelated note by a different author on a different topic — so this summary is based only on the title, technote number, and known metadata rather than verified content about V6 cross-platform strategies. Based on the title alone, cross-platform (Mac/Windows) development guidance was a real and recurring concern in the 4D V6 era given differences in fonts, screen resolution, and file systems between the two platforms, a topic still conceptually relevant, though any 1996 V6-specific guidance would be superseded by decades of subsequent cross-platform tooling improvements.
related_updates: The archived extraction for this specific asset is not usable — it duplicates the content of a different Tech Note (96-50, Remote Access), so no specific V6 cross-platform recommendations can be verified from source

4D's modern cross-platform development model (a single shared structure file running natively on Mac and Windows via the same IDE) has evolved enormously since V6-era Mac/Windows font and display differences were a major concern
